newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Water Power expands wholesale sales.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Water Power expands wholesale sales.

text.p: Washington Water Power (WWP) sold a record 4.55 million megawatt hours (MWh) of wholesale power during the first six months of this year, the Spokane, Washington utility said Thursday.
The contracts represent $90 million in revenue, said Lloyd Meyers, wholesale marketing manager at WWP.
"Only four power marketers in the nation sold more wholesale megawatts in the first half of 1996 than WWP," he noted.
"We sold 2.6 million MWh to wholesale customers versus 1.6 million MWh in retail. And we estimate that we'll be running close to 50 percent more megawatts than retail for the remainder of 1996."

The nation's top power marketers as ranked by sales for the first half of 1996 include: Enron Corp, with sales of 21.4 million MWh; LG&E Energy Corp subsidiary Louisville Gas & Electric at 5.7 million MWh; Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp with 4.7 million MWh; and NGC Corp subsidiary Electric Clearinghouse at 4.6 million MWh sold.
In a move designed to promote the future growth of its wholesale business, WWP sought and was awarded Wednesday national power marketer certification by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
The company said it will join the growing ranks of FERC approved national power marketers by launching a subsidiary company, WWP Resource Services, later this year.
